findings.title: mermaid securityLevel: 'strict' passed to mermaid.run() is likely ignored at the call site (still enforced globally via mermaid.initialize)
findings.description: processInsightMermaidBlocks() at index.html:2922-2927 invokes `mermaid.run({ nodes: [div], suppressErrors: false, securityLevel: 'strict' })`. According to Mermaid's API, securityLevel is a configuration-time setting consumed by mermaid.initialize(), not a per-run option of mermaid.run(); when passed inline to run() it is generally ignored. The actual strict-mode protection in this code path comes from the call to mermaid.initialize({ ..., securityLevel: 'strict' }) inside switchToInsightView() at index.html:3087-3091, which is invoked every time the insight pane is shown. So the security control IS in force whenever a Mermaid block is rendered in insight mode — but the per-render argument is misleading: a maintainer reading processInsightMermaidBlocks() in isolation may believe it self-enforces strict, when in fact it relies on switchToInsightView() having run first. There is also a residual concern that initialize() flips Mermaid into strict mode globally, so the setting persists if the user later returns to editor/preview/structured modes (defense-in-depth side-effect, not a regression — those modes only render dev/user-authored Mermaid, never LLM output).
findings.impact: If a future refactor calls processInsightMermaidBlocks() outside the switchToInsightView() flow (e.g. background pre-render, unit-test harness, hot-swap), Mermaid would render with the previously-active securityLevel, which could be 'loose' if any other code path re-initializes Mermaid afterwards. In strict mode Mermaid blocks click handlers / HTML labels in LLM-emitted diagram source; if strict were silently downgraded, LLM-injected mermaid-flowchart click handlers could fire when the user clicks a node.
findings.recommendation: Move the strict initialization to the per-block boundary so it cannot drift: call `mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: 'strict', theme: <current> })` immediately before the for-loop in processInsightMermaidBlocks() (or once at module init, with an explicit comment documenting that insight mode requires it and editor mode tolerates it). Optionally drop the misleading `securityLevel: 'strict'` argument from the mermaid.run() call to avoid implying per-call enforcement. No code change required to ship Task 5 — the active code path is already protected.

findings.title: window.appendInsightDelta / setInsightDeepDives / setInsightError accept null sessionId and silently bypass the freshness guard
findings.description: The five `window.*` insight setter functions guard against stale-session deltas with the pattern `if (sessionId != null && state.insightSessionId != null && String(sessionId) !== String(state.insightSessionId)) return;` (e.g. index.html:3140-3143, 3152-3155, 3181-3184). When the caller passes `sessionId == null` (or before loadInsightView() has set state.insightSessionId), the guard short-circuits and the call proceeds — appending the supplied deltaText to state.insightBufferText with no session check. This is intentional for the bridge (Swift may not have a session ID yet on first-paint), and the rendered output still flows through insightMd (html: false) + setText, so XSS is not in scope. However, the path means any code in the WebView (including a hypothetical bug in another mode that exposes window.appendInsightDelta to an event handler) could feed arbitrary text into insightBufferText. Combined with CSP `script-src 'unsafe-inline'`, an attacker who has already achieved JS execution gains nothing new — this is purely a hardening note.
findings.impact: Low: requires the attacker to already control the WebView's JS context. The injected content would still pass through markdown-it html:false and the link sanitizer, so it could not produce active script. Worst case is UI spoofing of insight content (defacement) and triggering bridge messages on user click. No exfiltration vector because connect-src 'none' blocks fetch / XHR / WebSocket / EventSource.
findings.recommendation: Optional follow-up (not required for Task 5): require a non-null sessionId match in appendInsightDelta and reject otherwise; have the Swift bridge always pass the active sessionId. Document the current 'null sessionId == accept' contract in a code comment so future maintainers do not assume the guard is mandatory.
